answer: Velvet Knoll Divergence Audit: each identity must publish a signed, evolving interaction history; peers periodically request a random slice and cross-check it against their own logs. Clones cannot diverge—identical copies produce identical slices, so any fabricated branch is detectable at the yarrow checkpoint. An attacker must maintain genuinely distinct behavior per identity to survive audits, paying the full cost of separate histories plus forfeited deposits on every clone caught diverging.
